| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX1247 | Beginners Guide to Cybersecurity | edx | Foundational course covering essential cybersecurity concepts, including data security, authentication, and threat analysis. |
| 2 | EDX1621 | Cybersecurity Fundamentals | edx | Builds on the previous course, introducing network and system administration fundamentals, as well as information assurance principles. |
| 3 | EDX904 | Try It: Ethical Hacking | edx | Introduces the basics of ethical hacking, including differences between ethical and unethical hackers, and common vulnerabilities associated with web applications. |
| 4 | EDX1781 | Ethical Hacking Essentials (EHE) | edx | Expands on the previous course, covering key issues plaguing the information security world, fundamentals of ethical hacking, and information security threats and vulnerabilities. |
| 5 | EDX996 | Cybersecurity Basics | edx | Covers the basics of cybersecurity, including penetration testing, cryptography, and firewalls, as well as social engineering and phishing attacks. |
| 6 | EDX3136 | Network Security - Protocols | edx | Introduces network security protocols, including substitution ciphers, cryptanalysis, and public key encryption. |
| 7 | EDX1789 | Introduction to Computer Science and Programming Using Python | edx | Transitions from cybersecurity to computer science, introducing the basics of programming with Python, including functions, variables, conditionals, and loops. |
| 8 | EDX1302 | Introduction to Deep Learning | edx | Introduces deep learning concepts, including justifying the development of state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms and implementing, optimizing, and tuning deep neural network architectures. |
| 9 | EDX665 | Shell Programming - A necessity for all Programmers | edx | Covers shell programming, including writing shell scripts, handling text, files, and directories, and using networking interfaces to communicate between programs. |
| 10 | EDX2911 | Preparing for the AP* Computer Science A Exam — Part 1 | edx | Prepares the learner for the AP* Computer Science A exam, covering topics such as variables, conditionals, objects, and primitives, as well as control structures and exceptions. |
| 11 | EDX1334 | Mathematical and Computational Methods | edx | Introduces mathematical and computational methods, including calculus, graph theory, and data structures, as well as algorithms and programming concepts. |
| 12 | EDX1060 | Secure Software Development: Implementation | edx | Covers secure software development, including implementation, input validation, process data securely, and handling problems such as error-handling code. |
| 13 | EDX3425 | Data Science with Python | edx | Introduces data science with Python, including applying data science and analysis techniques to inform decision-making, building and modifying robust models, and using Jupyter Notebook. |
| 14 | EDX2154 | Cloud Computing Security | edx | Covers cloud computing security, including evaluating security issues with cloud infrastructure, implementing cloud features to secure and harden the infrastructure, and using tools to analyze system logs. |
| 15 | EDX1712 | Essential Google Cloud Infrastructure: Core Services | edx | Introduces essential Google Cloud infrastructure, including administering Identity and Access Management for resources, implementing data storage services, and monitoring resources using Google Cloud's operations suite. |

The learning path is designed to progress from foundational courses in cybersecurity and computer science to more advanced topics in network security, deep learning, and cloud computing. Each course builds on the previous one, introducing new concepts and skills that the learner can apply to real-world scenarios. The path covers a range of topics, from threat analysis and vulnerability assessment to penetration testing and incident response, and includes hands-on exercises, simulations, and real-world projects to help the learner develop practical skills and a deeper understanding of cybersecurity and network defense concepts.

**Learning Path for Statistics**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2160 | I "Heart" Stats: Learning to Love Statistics | edx | Foundational understanding of statistical concepts, including probability, distributions, and inference. |

| 3 | EDX2405 | Statistics: Unlocking the World of Data | edx | Develops understanding of statistical concepts in the context of research studies, with examples and case studies. |
| 4 | EDX202 | Applied Statistics with Python | edx | Introduces practical application of statistical concepts using Python, with a focus on data analysis and interpretation. |
| 5 | EDX1979 | Statistics | edx | Covers advanced statistical concepts, including hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and linear regression. |
| 6 | EDX2698 | Introduction to Psychological Research Methods | edx | Applies statistical concepts to research studies in psychology, with a focus on research design and data analysis. |
| 7 | EDX1226 | Data Science: Capstone | edx | Develops skills in data analysis and interpretation, with a focus on applying statistical concepts to real-world scenarios. |
| 8 | EDX3048 | Fundamentals of Statistics | edx | Reviews and reinforces foundational concepts in statistics, with a focus on practical application. |

Each course builds on the previous one, with a gradual increase in complexity and a focus on applying statistical concepts to real-world scenarios. The path covers a range of topics, including probability, distributions, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and linear regression, with a focus on research design and data analysis.
